research_notes.finding:
Current store uses Zustand persist middleware with localStorage. Pattern works but lacks: - IndexedDB durability - Complex query capability - Larger storage capacity
Migration path: Replace storage adapter, keep store actions.

Working Dexie integration exists in useProviderStore: 1. Uses createJSONStorage wrapper around createDexieStorage 2. Has partialize to select which state to persist 3. Has onRehydrateStorage for defaults/cleanup 4. Integrates with credentialVault for secure key handling
This is the target pattern for agents-store migration.
Dexie supports navigator.storage.persist() for durability. IndexedDB storage is more resilient than localStorage. Automatic schema versioning with upgrade migrations.

Decision: Zustand + Dexie Middleware (Option A) - Solving BF-01 (hot-reload) and BF-02 (atomic updates) - Pattern: persist middleware with Dexie storage adapter - partialize for selective field persistence

architecture_patterns.pattern: All state through Zustand → Dexie middleware. Components subscribe to Zustand selectors, never direct Dexie.
Components → Zustand → Dexie (never skip layers). State mutations always through store actions.
1. Save previous state 2. Apply optimistic update (immediate UI) 3. Persist async 4. Rollback on error
Export usexxxStoreHydration() hook. Components can wait for IndexedDB restoration before rendering.
All UI strings through i18next. Add keys to en.json and vi.json.

technical_notes.note: API keys NEVER go in agent store state directly. Always use credentialVault for encrypted storage. Store only reference (agentId/providerId) in main state.
Follow provider-store.ts pattern EXACTLY: 1. createJSONStorage wrapper 2. createDexieStorage with table name 3. partialize for selective persistence 4. onRehydrateStorage for defaults
Add Dexie schema version 7 BEFORE changing store. Schema upgrade runs automatically on db.open(). Test migration with existing v6 data.
Mock dexie-storage in unit tests (see provider-store.test.ts). Test hydration timing with performance.now(). Target: <100ms for 10 agents.
New table name: 'agentConfigs' (not 'agents' - too generic) New store name: 'agent-configs' (matches table)
useConversationStore will follow same pattern. Table: 'conversationState' Store name: 'conversation-state'
